prompt: An interface is started with /PS=O. Which PI point attribute must be set to O so the interface loads the point?

options.text: PointSource
Location1
InstrumentTag
PointClass

explanation: The PointSource attribute must match the value set by the interface's /PS parameter. Location1 usually matches /ID (the instance), InstrumentTag holds a source address on some interfaces, and PointClass has nothing to do with which interface owns the point.

prompt: Which point attribute typically assigns a PI point to one of the interface's /f scan classes?

options.text: Location1
Location4
Location5
Scan

explanation: Location4 is typically the scan class number (/f). Location1 is typically the interface instance (/ID). The Scan attribute only switches scanning on or off and should always be ON for interface points.

prompt: Which statement about the PI Interface Configuration Utility (PI ICU) is correct?

options.text: It can configure interfaces on any computer in the domain
It can only configure PI Interfaces that run on the same computer as PI ICU
It stores the configuration only in the batch file, never on the Data Archive
It replaces the batch file with an XML configuration file

explanation: PI ICU can only configure interfaces on its own computer. It is a GUI for the startup batch file and also writes the configuration to the Module Database on the Data Archive, which allows recovery. The batch file remains the interface's configuration.

prompt: Put the steps a PI Interface follows to collect data in order.

items.text: Read the value from the data source
Send it to the PI Data Archive

explanation: AVEVA's administration course lists interface data collection as read, timestamp, format, apply exception, send. Exception is applied before sending, which is why it saves network traffic.

prompt: Which of these does the UniInt framework provide to interfaces built on it? Select all that apply.

options.text: Orderly startup and shutdown, and messaging
Automatic handling of PI point attribute changes
Failover
Bad-data and comms-failure indication
Swinging-door compression on the Data Archive
Asset Framework template creation

explanation: UniInt gives a consistent installation, similar parameters, orderly startup and shutdown, messaging, bad-data and comms-failure indication, automatic handling of point attribute changes, and failover. Swinging-door compression runs in the Snapshot Subsystem (or the buffer), and creating AF templates is not a UniInt feature.

prompt: Match each interface startup parameter to what it means.

pairs.right: Point source: which interface owns a point
Interface ID: which instance of the interface
Scan class: how often to read a value
The name of the PI server

explanation: The architecture course describes /PS as "which interface?", /ID as "which instance of the interface?" and /F as "how often to read a value?". /HOST is the name of the PI server.

prompt: The scan class /f=00:01:00,00:00:05 can also be written in seconds as /f=___ . Type the value after the equals sign.
explanation: 00:01:00 is a 60-second period and 00:00:05 is a 5-second offset, so /f=60,5 is equivalent. Scans then run at reference time + n x frequency + offset.

prompt: What does the ,L at the end of /f=24:00:00,00:08:00,L do?

options.text: Marks the scan class as low priority
Tells UniInt to use wall-clock scheduling, so the daily 08:00 scan stays at 08:00 across daylight-saving changes
Writes the scan results to the local log file
Limits the scan class to output points

explanation: ",L" tells UniInt to use the wall-clock scheduling algorithm, which keeps a daily 08:00 local scan steady when clocks change for daylight saving.

scenario: An OT engineer puts 200 polled points and 50 advise points into scan class 1 of the same interface instance. Update rates become erratic and some advise points look stale.

options.text: Move the advise points to their own scan class so advise and polled points are not mixed
Raise the scan frequency of scan class 1 to one second
Set the Scan attribute of the advise points to OFF
Change the advise points' PointSource to a new letter without changing /PS

explanation: AVEVA's guidance is "Do not mix advised points and polled points in the same group (i.e., scan class)." Turning Scan off stops collection entirely, and a PointSource that no longer matches /PS means the interface will not load the points.

prompt: How far off the server clock can an interface node's clock be before the interface will not run?

options.text: More than 30 seconds
More than 10 minutes
More than 30 minutes
Clock differences never matter because timestamps are UTC

explanation: An interface whose clock is more than 30 minutes off the server clock will not run. The 10-minute figure is a different rule: real-time values timestamped more than 10 minutes in the future are discarded. UTC timestamps do not remove the need for accurate clocks.

prompt: Which UniInt health points does the PI System administration course recommend creating? Select all that apply.

options.text: Heartbeat
Device Status
IO Rate
Scan Class Scans Skipped
Archive Compression Ratio
Snapshot Queue Length

explanation: The recommended health points, created in PI ICU under UniInt > Health Points, are Heartbeat, Device Status, IO Rate and Scan Class Scans Skipped. The other two are not UniInt health points.

prompt: Which statement about UniInt disconnected startup is correct?

options.text: The very first start can be done without any Data Archive connection
Outputs continue to be written while disconnected
The first startup must connect; afterwards the interface can start from its point and digital-set cache files
It is only meant for test systems and is not recommended for production

explanation: Disconnected startup needs one connected start to create the point-cache and digital-set-cache files. After that the interface can start without the Data Archive. Outputs are not supported while disconnected, and AVEVA recommends the feature for production.

prompt: An interface built on UniInt 4.5.0.x writes its messages where?

options.text: To the PI Message Log
Only to PIPC\dat\pipc.log
To the Windows Application event log only
To a SQL Server table

explanation: Interfaces with UniInt 4.5.0.x or later write to the PI Message Log, which pigetmsg -f shows continuously. Interfaces with UniInt earlier than 2.5.0.x write to pipc.log.

scenario: Your security team wants every new interface service to run under a group managed service account (gMSA). You open PI ICU to create the service for a new instance.

options.text: Enter the gMSA in the ICU Service tab and create the service
Create the service in ICU under the default NT Service account, then switch it to the gMSA in Services Manager
Run the interface interactively under the gMSA instead of as a service
Map a PI Trust to piadmin so the account does not matter

explanation: PI ICU cannot create a service under a gMSA. Create it under the default NT Service account, then change the logon account in Services Manager. Interactive runs are for testing only, and trusts should never map to piadmin.
